subject: ela
intro: When we read informational text, we use both the words AND the pictures together. Illustrations, diagrams, and photos show us things that are hard to describe with only words. This skill teaches students to look at both the text and the image to fully understand the key ideas.

items.prompt:
Read the text and look at the image described below.

Text: 'Butterflies have wings. They use their wings to fly.'

Image: A diagram shows a butterfly with two large wings on each side of its body. Arrows point to each wing.

What does the image show that the words do not tell you?

steps: I read the text. It tells me butterflies have wings and use them to fly.
I look at the image. It shows the butterfly has two large wings on EACH SIDE, and arrows point to each wing.
The words say 'wings' but do not say how many or where they are on the body.
The image adds the detail that there are two wings on each side.
solution.answer: The image shows that the butterfly has two large wings on each side of its body. The words only say 'wings' but do not tell us how many or where they are placed.

items.prompt:
Read the text and look at the image described below.

Text: 'A fire truck is red. Firefighters ride in it to help people.'

Image: A photo shows a bright red fire truck with a long ladder on top and a hose coiled on the side.

What key idea does the image help you understand?

steps: I read the text. It tells me the truck is red and firefighters ride in it.
I look at the image. It shows a ladder on top and a hose on the side.
The words do not mention the ladder or the hose.
The image helps me understand that fire trucks carry special tools to fight fires.
solution.answer: The image helps me understand that fire trucks carry special equipment like a ladder and a hose. The words only say the truck is red and carries firefighters.

items.prompt:
Read the text and look at the image described below.

Text: 'Sunflowers grow tall. They turn to face the sun.'

Image: A drawing shows a sunflower with a long green stem, large yellow petals around a dark brown center, and the sun shining to the right while the flower faces toward it.

What information comes from the image that is not in the words?

steps: I read the text. It tells me sunflowers grow tall and turn to face the sun.
I look at the image. It shows yellow petals around a dark brown center and a green stem.
The words do not describe the colors or what a sunflower looks like.
The image shows me the shape and colors of the sunflower.
solution.answer: The image shows the sunflower's yellow petals, dark brown center, and green stem. The words only tell me it grows tall and faces the sun, but do not describe what it looks like.

items.prompt:
Read the text and look at the image described below.

Text: 'Frogs start as eggs. Then they grow into tadpoles. Finally, they become frogs.'

Image: A diagram shows three boxes with arrows between them. Box 1 shows a cluster of frog eggs. Box 2 shows a tadpole with a long tail. Box 3 shows a frog with four legs.

How does the image help you understand the text?

steps: I read the text. It tells me frogs go through three stages: eggs, tadpoles, then frogs.
I look at the image. It shows pictures of each stage in order with arrows connecting them.
The image helps me see what each stage looks like.
Together, the text names the stages and the image shows what each stage looks like.
solution.answer: The image helps me see exactly what each stage looks like. The text names the stages in order, and the diagram shows a picture of eggs, a tadpole, and a frog so I can see how a frog changes.

items.prompt:
Read the text and look at the image described below.

Text: 'Rain clouds form when water goes up into the sky. The clouds get heavy and rain falls down.'

Image: A diagram shows arrows going up from a lake to a cloud, then drops of rain falling down from the cloud to the ground.

What key idea does the image add to the text?

steps: I read the text. It tells me water goes up to form clouds, then rain falls down.
I look at the image. It shows arrows going UP from a lake and then rain coming DOWN.
The image shows the direction water travels, which helps me understand the cycle.
The image makes the up-and-down movement clear in a way that is easy to follow.
solution.answer: The image adds the idea of movement, showing arrows going up from water and rain coming back down. This makes the water cycle much easier to picture than the words alone.

items.prompt:
Read the text and look at the image described below.

Text: 'Dogs make good pets. They are friendly and loyal.'

Image: A photo shows a dog sitting next to a child, wagging its tail, with the child's hand on the dog's back.

What does the image show that adds to the words?
items.hint: Look at what is happening in the picture that the words do not say.

steps: I read the text. It says dogs are friendly and loyal.
I look at the image. It shows a dog sitting with a child, wagging its tail.
The words say dogs are friendly, but the image shows a friendly moment between a dog and a child.
The image gives a real example of a dog being friendly.
solution.answer: The image shows a real example of a friendly dog sitting beside a child and wagging its tail. The words say dogs are friendly, and the image proves it by showing a friendly moment.

items.prompt:
Read the text and look at the image described below.

Text: 'The moon has craters on its surface.'

Image: A photo shows a round moon with many circles of different sizes on its surface.

What key idea does the image help you understand?
items.hint: Think about what 'craters' look like. Do the words describe them? Does the image show them?

steps: I read the text. It tells me the moon has craters.
I look at the image. It shows many circles of different sizes on the moon.
The words say craters are there but do not describe what they look like.
The image shows that craters are bowl-shaped holes of different sizes.
solution.answer: The image helps me understand what craters look like. The words tell me craters are on the moon, but the image shows they are round, bowl-shaped holes of different sizes.

items.prompt:
Read the text and look at the image described below.

Text: 'Bees live together in a hive. They work as a team.'

Image: A diagram shows the inside of a beehive with rows of six-sided cells. Some cells are filled with honey. Many bees are crawling on the cells.

What information does the image give that the words leave out?
items.hint: Look at the shape of the cells in the hive. Do the words mention that?

steps: I read the text. It says bees live in a hive and work as a team.
I look at the image. It shows six-sided cells inside the hive and honey in some of them.
The words do not describe the shape of the cells or the honey inside.
The image shows that the hive is made of six-sided cells and that bees store honey there.
solution.answer: The image shows that the inside of a hive is made of six-sided cells and that some cells are filled with honey. The words only say bees live in a hive and work as a team.

items.prompt:
Read the text and look at the image described below.

Text: 'A seed needs water, soil, and sunlight to grow into a plant.'

Image: A diagram shows a seed in the soil with arrows pointing to it labeled 'water,' 'sunlight,' and 'soil.' A sprout grows up from the seed.

How does the image work together with the text?
items.hint: Think about which parts of the image match the words and what the image shows that the words do not.

steps: I read the text. It names three things a seed needs: water, soil, and sunlight.
I look at the image. It shows each of those three things with arrows pointing to the seed.
The image also shows a sprout growing, which the text does not describe.
Together, the words name the needs and the image shows all three pointing toward a growing plant.
solution.answer: The image works with the text by showing labeled arrows for water, sunlight, and soil pointing to the seed. It also shows a sprout growing up, which gives me a picture of the seed turning into a plant.

items.prompt:
Read the text and look at the image described below.

Text: 'A community helper is a person who helps others in the neighborhood. Police officers, teachers, and doctors are community helpers.'

Image: Three photos show a police officer in a blue uniform, a teacher pointing to a board, and a doctor in a white coat.

What does the image help you understand about the key idea?
items.hint: Think about why the author chose to show three different photos.

steps: I read the text. It defines community helpers and lists three examples.
I look at the image. It shows a picture of each of the three helpers mentioned.
The image helps me see what each community helper looks like and how they dress for their job.
The words give the names and the image shows what each one looks like in real life.
solution.answer: The image helps me understand what each community helper looks like. The words name three helpers, and the photos show each one in their uniform or work setting so I can recognize them.
